note: Real segmentation as the business runs it. Replaces the previously invented ICP text.
source: Grace Hill sales and CS segmentation definitions; RML Pricing & Packaging Baseline Analysis, July 2026

sales.label: Sales segmentation
sales.basis: Total portfolio units, plus account status

outcomeSegments.label: Outcome segments
outcomeSegments.why: More useful for positioning than unit count, because it describes what the customer is trying to do. Segments 2–5 all serve one goal: NOI.

rows.name: Compliance Seeker
rows.note: Largest segment by customer count, smallest by products held. The obvious cross-sell pool.

rows.name: Market Intelligence Seeker
rows.note: Fastest growing at 150%, and mostly arriving as new logos.

rows.name: Sentiment Seeker
rows.note: Small. Survey churn is driven by the product feeling dated, not by price.

rows.name: Power User
rows.wants: Two or more of the above
rows.note: 12% of customers, 48% of MRR. Five of the six migration paths end here.

migration.label: How customers actually expand
points: Almost every path ends at Power User — five of the six transitions.
Mystery Shopping and HelloData® are what customers add. Training or Policies is usually the front door.
The single biggest move: Training-only customers adding Mystery Shopping — 52 of them.
Power User is reached in steps, not one jump. Expansion has to be designed as a ladder.

whyWeLose.label: Why we actually lose
whyWeLose.headline: On consolidation and value — not on price.
points: 75% of lost revenue is winnable or fixable. Only 25% is structural: M&A, portfolio sold, business closed.
Price is among the smallest real drivers at 11% of churned MRR.
Training and Policies lose to tech-stack consolidation. Yardi is the name that comes up.
Surveys lose because the product feels dated — lack of innovation is the top stated reason, not cost.
Mystery Shopping loses to "no longer a strategic priority" and portfolio reduction.
whyWeLose.useIt: When someone says they are consolidating vendors, that is the single largest reason we lose. Do not treat it as a price conversation.
